blocks.text: Use places for multi-scene worlds. Main world is places.main.
Each place can define terrain, atmosphere, objects, default spawn point, and default spawn rotation.
defaultPlace controls where new players spawn (defaults to "main").

GameSpec = { buyables?: Record<string, BuyableDef> // Buyable registry (buyableId -> buyable definition) achievements?: Record<string, AchievementDef> // Achievements Spawn lists on the game's page (milestone name -> achievement) leaderboards?: Record<string, LeaderboardDef> // Boards Spawn ranks on the game's page (board id -> the player.state row it ranks) inputs?: InputsDef // Input bindings player?: PlayerDef // Player template camera?: CameraDef // Camera configuration material?: MaterialSpec // The base every object's `material` merges over per key: a bare object wears it whole, `{ texture }` keeps its roughness under the texture, an explicit material wins on every key it names; a place's own stands over it. Absent, nothing merges. lighting?: string // The lighting function's file: `"scripts/lighting.js"`, exporting lighting(surface, lights) → the colour of every lit surface; a place's own stands over it. Absent, the engine's standard model. sky?: string // The sky function's file: `"scripts/sky.js"`, exporting sky(ray, world) → the sky's colour per direction, drawn by the dome and the light's capture alike; a place's own stands over it. Absent, the engine's physical sky. Its terms are the physical sky's own, as builtin/tsl nodes: ray.direction; world.atmosphere (the day sky, no sun disc), world.night (the moon, the stars, the moonlit wash), world.clouds() (the cloud layer as straight rgba: .rgb lit, .a cover), world.sun and world.moon (.direction, .radiance, .disc(size)), world.param(name, default). audio?: WorldAudioPolicy // The game's mix under the player's sliders: gains per bus, the voice budget, the cull distance (`spawn api WorldAudioPolicy`). Absent, the engine's defaults. passThrough?: Record<string, string[]> // Which collision layers pass through which: `{ car: ["car"] }` (a body names its layer with `physics.layer`). A pair passes both ways; "player" always passes through "player", and every other pair not named collides. ui?: GameUIDef // UI overlay godMode?: GodModeConfig // God mode configuration. creatorUi?: UIDef // Creator UI overlay (engine-injected, mounted during god mode). deprecated: Superseded by `creatorTabs`. No longer compiled into the god-mode rail (hard-cut in the creator-tabs version); migrate via the engine version's migrationNotes. creatorTabs?: CreatorTabDef[] // God-mode authoring tabs (top-right rail), in rail order; a mod's tab (its mod.json `tab`) is not listed. Each starts closed until the creator presses it. engine?: EngineConfig // Engine configuration (networking) routing?: RoutingDef // Room routing: names a pickRoom(ctx) script and the per-room player cap places?: Record<string, PlaceDef> // Places (NEW) defaultPlace?: string // Default place for new players (default: "main") earshot?: number // Earshot in metres: how far a voice carries, and above ten players a said line and a nameplate. With ten or fewer players a said line reaches the whole room, a nameplate stands over everyone in the viewer's place, and a voice reaches the whole room until chat.js has a voice room. Default 40 when absent. A town square wants it wide, a whisper game tight. voiceMood?: "cave" | "hall" | "open" // The room's voice mood; the reverb every heard voice wears in this world: `cave` (long and wet), `hall` (a room's bloom), `open` (dry; the default when absent). One word, nothing in the UI. nameplates?: boolean // Names over other players' heads, within earshot. Default true; false hides every one: hide-and-seek, horror. voice?: boolean // Voice chat between players in this world. Default true; false turns it off: nobody can join voice here (a menu game, a quiet puzzle). nametag?: string // The tag over other players' heads as a render file in this tree (every starter ships `ui/nametag.js`): `export default function (ctx, tag) { return html }`: the shape `ui.js` has, called per tag when its facts move or what it reads through `ctx` moves, `<style>` rides the string; absent, the engine's default: the same file. chat?: string // The world's chat file: `"scripts/chat.js"`, exporting `scopes` (a channel = who is in it and who may post: `{ trade: { in: (ctx, p) => …, post: (ctx, p) => …, slow, waits } }`, code over the player's rows), `character` (the player.state row shown as the name on the tag) and `profile` (at most four player.state rows, one dim line under it). Absent, chat is `say` alone. assets?: { // Asset metadata cache: persisted per-model derived data (bounds, semantic sockets) for CDN models, refreshed when extraction semantics change. metadata?: Record<string, AssetMetadata> authoredClips?: Record<string, AuthoredClipEntry | null> // A 5.x document's script-authored animation clips, keyed by identity (`<scriptRef>#<fnName>` / `tracks#<name>`): sampled keyframe tracks. A 6.0 world keeps each clip as its own file under clips/; the conversion writes one file per entry and none for a `null` (an identity a sweep evicted). } }

GameSpec = {
  buyables?: Record<string, BuyableDef>   // Buyable registry (buyableId -> buyable definition)
  achievements?: Record<string, AchievementDef>   // Achievements Spawn lists on the game's page (milestone name -> achievement)
  leaderboards?: Record<string, LeaderboardDef>   // Boards Spawn ranks on the game's page (board id -> the player.state row it ranks)
  inputs?: InputsDef   // Input bindings
  player?: PlayerDef   // Player template
  camera?: CameraDef   // Camera configuration
  material?: MaterialSpec   // The base every object's `material` merges over per key: a bare object wears it whole, `{ texture }` keeps its roughness under the texture, an explicit material wins on every key it names; a place's own stands over it. Absent, nothing merges.
  lighting?: string   // The lighting function's file: `"scripts/lighting.js"`, exporting lighting(surface, lights) → the colour of every lit surface; a place's own stands over it. Absent, the engine's standard model.
  sky?: string   // The sky function's file: `"scripts/sky.js"`, exporting sky(ray, world) → the sky's colour per direction, drawn by the dome and the light's capture alike; a place's own stands over it. Absent, the engine's physical sky. Its terms are the physical sky's own, as builtin/tsl nodes: ray.direction; world.atmosphere (the day sky, no sun disc), world.night (the moon, the stars, the moonlit wash), world.clouds() (the cloud layer as straight rgba: .rgb lit, .a cover), world.sun and world.moon (.direction, .radiance, .disc(size)), world.param(name, default).
  audio?: WorldAudioPolicy   // The game's mix under the player's sliders: gains per bus, the voice budget, the cull distance (`spawn api WorldAudioPolicy`). Absent, the engine's defaults.
  passThrough?: Record<string, string[]>   // Which collision layers pass through which: `{ car: ["car"] }` (a body names its layer with `physics.layer`). A pair passes both ways; "player" always passes through "player", and every other pair not named collides.
  ui?: GameUIDef   // UI overlay
  godMode?: GodModeConfig   // God mode configuration.
  creatorUi?: UIDef   // Creator UI overlay (engine-injected, mounted during god mode). deprecated: Superseded by `creatorTabs`. No longer compiled into the god-mode rail (hard-cut in the creator-tabs version); migrate via the engine version's migrationNotes.
  creatorTabs?: CreatorTabDef[]   // God-mode authoring tabs (top-right rail), in rail order; a mod's tab (its mod.json `tab`) is not listed. Each starts closed until the creator presses it.
  engine?: EngineConfig   // Engine configuration (networking)
  routing?: RoutingDef   // Room routing: names a pickRoom(ctx) script and the per-room player cap
  places?: Record<string, PlaceDef>   // Places (NEW)
  defaultPlace?: string   // Default place for new players (default: "main")
  earshot?: number   // Earshot in metres: how far a voice carries, and above ten players a said line and a nameplate. With ten or fewer players a said line reaches the whole room, a nameplate stands over everyone in the viewer's place, and a voice reaches the whole room until chat.js has a voice room. Default 40 when absent. A town square wants it wide, a whisper game tight.
  voiceMood?: "cave" | "hall" | "open"   // The room's voice mood; the reverb every heard voice wears in this world: `cave` (long and wet), `hall` (a room's bloom), `open` (dry; the default when absent). One word, nothing in the UI.
  nameplates?: boolean   // Names over other players' heads, within earshot. Default true; false hides every one: hide-and-seek, horror.
  voice?: boolean   // Voice chat between players in this world. Default true; false turns it off: nobody can join voice here (a menu game, a quiet puzzle).
  nametag?: string   // The tag over other players' heads as a render file in this tree (every starter ships `ui/nametag.js`): `export default function (ctx, tag) { return html }`: the shape `ui.js` has, called per tag when its facts move or what it reads through `ctx` moves, `<style>` rides the string; absent, the engine's default: the same file.
  chat?: string   // The world's chat file: `"scripts/chat.js"`, exporting `scopes` (a channel = who is in it and who may post: `{ trade: { in: (ctx, p) => …, post: (ctx, p) => …, slow, waits } }`, code over the player's rows), `character` (the player.state row shown as the name on the tag) and `profile` (at most four player.state rows, one dim line under it). Absent, chat is `say` alone.
  assets?: {   // Asset metadata cache: persisted per-model derived data (bounds, semantic sockets) for CDN models, refreshed when extraction semantics change.
    metadata?: Record<string, AssetMetadata>
    authoredClips?: Record<string, AuthoredClipEntry | null>   // A 5.x document's script-authored animation clips, keyed by identity (`<scriptRef>#<fnName>` / `tracks#<name>`): sampled keyframe tracks. A 6.0 world keeps each clip as its own file under clips/; the conversion writes one file per entry and none for a `null` (an identity a sweep evicted).
  }
}
